data.name: Tilly
data.gender_notes: Tilly is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Old English 'tilie' meaning 'rejoicing'. This name was common among the early English Christians. The name Tilly carries the meaning “Rejoicing Tilly” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Tilly usually hope their child will grow to embody rejoicing tilly and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that brings joy and hope in the Lord.
data.etymology: Tilly belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rejoicing Tilly.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tilly total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.
data.cultural_impact: The name Tilly gained popularity during the Middle Ages and the Elizabethan era. Its popularity is quite evident in the literary world, as several renowned authors such as William Shakespeare and John Webster featured characters named Tilly in their works.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Tilly holds significance in the Christian community as it is derived from the Old English 'tilie,' which means 'rejoicing.' The name is therefore an embodiment of joy, happiness, and celebration, which are all spiritual attributes. The name is believed to have been commonly bestowed upon children born during a joyous occasion or festivity, and as such, it serves as a constant reminder of the joy and happiness that comes from the Christian faith.
